title: Scalar and Vector Triple Products
notes: **Scalar triple product.** [a b c] = a · (b × c) is the signed volume of the parallelepiped on a, b, c; its absolute value is the volume, and one sixth of it is the tetrahedron volume.
**Coplanarity.** [a b c] = 0 exactly when the three vectors are coplanar; this is also the test for four points A, B, C, D being coplanar via AB, AC, AD.
**Determinant.** [a b c] equals the determinant of the 3 × 3 matrix with rows (or columns) a, b, c; swapping two rows changes the sign.
**Cyclic symmetry.** [a b c] = [b c a] = [c a b] and [a c b] = −[a b c]; the scalar triple product is unchanged by a cyclic permutation.
**Vector triple product.** a × (b × c) = (a·c)b − (a·b)c, the BAC − CAB identity; the result lies in the plane of b and c and is NOT associative.
**Exam caution.** a × (b × c) ≠ (a × b) × c in general; keep the parentheses and apply the identity to whichever pair is grouped.
summary: The scalar triple product a·(b×c) gives signed volume and tests coplanarity; the vector triple product expands as (a·c)b − (a·b)c.
